- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.40) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to prior high.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days — cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (e.g., 0.0–0.30), model underestimates mean reversion — adjust downward by 1–2% per 3-day horizon.
- When sentiment turns negative after a rally, model fails to recognize reversal — delay forecast drop by 1–2 days and reduce slope.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently overestimates near-term (1–7 day) volatility — smooth out early forecast spikes with 3-day moving average.
- If sentiment is positive and price is rising, model often overestimates continuation — reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3–5 days if sentiment > 0.20.
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 5+ days, model tends to underestimate true low — add 1–3% buffer to forecast lows.
- Model underestimates true price range when sentiment is volatile — widen forecast band by 1–2% if sentiment swings > ±0.30 in 3-day window.
